symptoms: You will see pale yellow or green streaks on the top of the leaves.
These streaks turn into brown spots that are shaped like an oval.
The middle of the spots turns light grey with a yellow ring around them.
The spots join together to create large patches of dry, dead leaf tissue.
The leaves dry out quickly and fall off the plant.
The fruit may stay small and thin even if the inside starts to ripen.
favourable_conditions: The disease spreads easily in poor, badly drained soils, shady areas, and during frequent irrigation.
prevention: Choose varieties that are known to be tolerant to this disease.
Do not plant your banana trees too close together.
Keep your field clean by removing weeds and grass.
Make sure your field has good drainage to stop water from sitting.
Use only healthy suckers that are free from disease for planting.
practices: Walk through your field regularly to check for early signs of the disease.
Cut off and destroy any leaves that show signs of the disease.
Remove extra suckers from the plant in a timely manner.
Keep the area around the plants free of weeds.
